To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) recurrent neural networks can learn compositional representations of sequences that can be approximated by tensor product representations, and (2) these representations are not robustly induced by existing tasks for learning sentence representations.

(a) RNNs implicitly implement TPRs; (b) the TPRs induced by RNNs trained on natural language tasks are largely approximated by a bag of words; (c) RNNs trained to encode natural language sentences do not induce robust TPR-based representations; and (d) TPR-based representations can be used to interpret the representations learned by RNNs.

we show that recurrent neural networks can learn compositional vector representations that are well approximated by tensor product representations, but that these representations are not induced in a way that is robust to changes in the data.

(i) RNNs can learn interpretable representations that can be well-approximated by tensor products; (ii) these representations can be learned by training on a variety of tasks, and can exhibit regularities; (iii) these regularities are not necessarily present in representations learned by training on natural language tasks.
